assertions.text: Table uses value-set syntax (curly braces like {READ, WRITE} or {READ, WRITE, DELETE}) to express rules that hold across multiple actions — rather than one row per role/action combination
assertions.evidence: {READ, WRITE, DELETE}, {WRITE, DELETE} value sets present in table

assertions.text: Table has fewer than 9 data rows (i.e. does not enumerate every role/action combination individually)
assertions.evidence: 6 data rows total (Admin, User read/write/delete, Guest read, Guest write/delete)

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: Scenario column is leftmost: 'Admin can perform any action', 'User can read', etc.

assertions.text: No two rows share both the same Role value and the same boolean output — forces value set consolidation

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case

If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as where permissions are checked in the request lifecycle, or open questions. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show. It is acceptable to omit @Description if the table already conveys all relevant context.
assertions.evidence: @Description omitted; analysis states 'table is fully self-explanatory'

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description absent, so assertion passes by default

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Admin performs any action', 'Guest reads') — not outcomes ('Allowed', 'Denied').
assertions.evidence: Scenarios: 'Admin can perform any action', 'User can read', 'Guest cannot write or delete'
